newsitem.title: USA: TRO Learning falls on flat Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: TRO Learning falls on flat Q4 results.

text.p: TRO Learning Inc shares fell almost 45 percent after the company said its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter revenues and profits fell short of expectations and that, as a result of the lower earnings, the company is in noncompliance with its loan agreement.

"As a result of the earnings shortfall the company is in technical noncompliance with certain of the financial covenants of its loan agreement," said William Roach, chairman and president, in a statement. "The company is seeking a waiver from its bank which it expects to receive," he added.
Shares of TRO Learning were trading off eight to 9-1/4.

Roach said the company did not meet all of the accounting requirements necessary to recognize the revenue surge at its Plato Education unit. The division saw orders for all of fiscal 1996 climb 56 percent to a record $39.5 million. However, Roach explained, the orders will only be treated as revenue as the Plato coursewear is distributed over the next three to 18 months. The company's offices are closed today.

"The company had a strong 1996 in terms of orders for its Plato coursewear," added Alexander Paris Jr., an analyst at Barrington Research Associates Inc, said. "Plato orders were up 56 percent and that's better than analysts expected."

"(Company management) said a few weeks ago there would be a delay in announcing fourth-quarter results and it was probably because of this issue," Paris continued, "Management probably wanted to report the orders as income, while the accountants said (the company) couldn't."

TRO Learning reported total revenues of $16.9 million in the fourth quarter, flat compared to the $16.8 million posted in 1995. Fourth-quarter earnings reached $2.3 million, down sharply from the $4.4 million the company reported in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Paris said TRO Learning executives told him a few weeeks ago the company is "well positioned in terms of people and product for the long term."
"They expect to count these orders as revenue as they're shipped over the next three to 18 months," Paris explained. "I don't think this is a material issue for the long term."
Paris said he expects more information when the company holds a conference call for analysts when its offices reopen Thursday.
TRO Learning develops computer-based interactive education software for schools, corporations and government programs.
